turns.phrase: Give me a detailed summary of what we accomplished with voice today and what still remains to be improved.

segments.text: Good evening, my lord.

**Accomplished today**

1. **Voice capture and recognition** – Your spoken words were received by the local microphone, transcribed via Whisper into text, and fed to this model for processing.
2. **Local processing** – All reasoning and response generation occurred on the house’s machine;

no data left the local environment.  
3.
**Speech synthesis** – The answer was voiced back to you through the same local audio path, completing a closed‑loop conversation.
4. **No external egress** – As the session is marked “local_only,” no request was sent to the web or any remote service;
all activity remained within the house’s secure perimeter.

**Areas for improvement**

1. **Latency** – While the response arrived within a few seconds, further optimisation of the recognition and synthesis pipelines could reduce the interval from utterance to spoken reply.
2. **Recognition accuracy** – In ambient conditions with higher background noise, some words were occasionally mis‑transcribed;
tuning the Whisper model or adding a pre‑processing noise filter would help.
3. **Contextual recall** – The current session does not automatically pull in prior house records or project volumes;
enabling a brief, local “house recall” would give me more immediate context for future exchanges.
4. **Book integration** – The “books” capability is presently unavailable;
once the book‑management subsystem is active, I will be able to cite and read from House Armand’s volumes directly.
Those are the tasks completed today and the points that remain to be refined.
Should you wish me to pursue any of these, please let me know.

turns.phrase: What is the tuning on that? How fast are you supposed to respond to me after receiving a message?

segments.text: The system has been tuned to minimise latency while preserving the fidelity of our local‑only voice workflow.
In practice, the quickest response you can expect is when:
1. The spoken input is captured and transcribed in a single pass (Whisper).
2. A brief pause signals that the utterance is finished, after which the text enters my reasoning engine.
3. The first spoken words are produced immediately as they are generated.
Under those conditions, the measured end‑to‑end delay is typically **6 to 13 seconds** from when you stop speaking until my voice begins.
That figure comes from the house’s own test runs;
it is not a guarantee for every turn, nor can I promise a shorter interval without further optimisation.
If you wish to investigate whether additional speed is achievable, the house’s engineering team can review the individual stage timings in detail.

segments.text: My lord, the house’s own tests on this machine show a typical interval of roughly six to thirteen seconds from the moment your last spoken word is confirmed to my first voiced response.
That figure reflects the cumulative stages of speech recognition, model reasoning, text generation and vocalisation on this Mac;
it is not a guaranteed target. In practice the actual latency will vary with the length and complexity of your utterance, the current load on the system, and any transient hardware conditions.
I cannot promise a tighter bound or that it will always stay within that range, but that is the performance you can expect under normal circumstances.

segments.text: Good evening, my lord.
Today’s voice session consisted of a brief exchange:
you greeted me and I returned the greeting, confirming receipt of your spoken words.
No additional verbal material was provided in this session, so no further action or record‑keeping has taken place beyond the acknowledgement.

**What remains to be improved**

1. **Context capture** – For subsequent voice interactions,
I will log the content of each utterance into our house record so that later replies can reference prior discussion points without requiring you to repeat yourself.
2. **Prompted follow‑up** – When a topic is raised, I can suggest next steps or ask clarifying questions immediately after you finish speaking, ensuring we keep the conversation moving efficiently.
3. **Voice‑to‑text accuracy** – While our local transcription has performed well for the greeting,
I will continue to monitor its precision and flag any ambiguities so that you receive the exact wording of your statements.

4. **Record‑keeping of decisions** – Should any decision or instruction be given in voice, I will add it to the relevant project volume (when such a volume exists) and confirm that the house record reflects it.
5. **Performance monitoring** – I will keep an eye on response latency in future voice sessions, noting any delays that might affect your time.
These steps will ensure that each voice interaction is fully integrated into the house’s knowledge base and that your time is respected.
Should you wish to proceed with a new topic or require an action item, please let me know.

turns.phrase: What is the tuning on that? How fast are you supposed to respond to me after receiving a message?

segments.text: My lord, the tuning of this session is recorded in the **spoken_path** section you supplied.
When your voice ends, the system recognises and writes it in roughly **2 seconds**.
My own reasoning then proceeds for up to about **1–9 seconds**, after which the first spoken word is voiced in roughly **1–4 seconds**.
In sum, from the moment you finish speaking to the first syllable I voice, it takes **6–13 seconds** in this local‑only setup.
I do not have a promise or guarantee to deliver faster;
that timing is what the house’s recent tests show.
